elements.author: urn:mock:organization:2414183
elements.commentary:
Three years ago we set ourselves a target that sounded slightly unreasonable at the time: every kilogram we roast would be traceable to the farm that grew it, and every farm would be paid above the reference price regardless of what the commodity market did that month.

We are not there yet. As of this quarter we are at 84% traceability by volume, up from 61% a year ago. The remaining 16% sits almost entirely in two blends where we buy through cooperatives that pool lots across dozens of smallholders — the coffee is excellent and the cooperatives are well run, but the paper trail stops at the mill.

What we learned along the way: traceability is a logistics problem long before it is an ethics problem. It needs someone at origin who can read a weighbridge ticket, and it needs a buyer willing to accept a smaller lot at a higher price.

Next year's target is 95%. We will publish the number either way, including the part where we miss it. {hashtag|\#|SpecialtyCoffee} {hashtag|\#|Traceability}
